# No Time to Hurry (Hiçbir Yere Yetişmeyenler Kulübü)

> A first-person field journal and small "club" by Murat Saydan that researches, tries out and
> honestly questions the philosophy of slow living: how to keep your own rhythm in the middle of
> work, the city and technology, without fleeing to the countryside. Bilingual (Turkish / English).
> No products for sale, no membership, no political aim and no hidden agenda — just one person
> recording his own "graph of change" as he learns to slow down.

## What "slow living" means here
Slow living is not doing everything slowly, and not escaping to a village. It is deciding for
yourself what to do and how fast — being a user of speed, not its captive. The site presents this
plainly: what slow living is, what it is not, who lives this way (slow food, slow fashion, digital
minimalism), whether it is sustainable (the Cittaslow / "slow city" movement, with its
gentrification and over-tourism contradictions), and the author's own honest, undecided stance.

## Core pages (English)
- [What is slow living?](https://notimetohurry.com/en/slow-living.html): The concept in plain language; the opposite of speed isn't slowness but connection (Hartmut Rosa).
- [Journal](https://notimetohurry.com/en/articles/index.html): Essays and field notes; each carries a cartoon.
- [Remembering How to Breathe in a World Doing a Billion Operations a Second](https://notimetohurry.com/en/articles/remembering-to-breathe.html): First piece — a technologist who can't keep up with AI; machine-speed vs. human-speed; from Seneca to Ivan Illich to Rosa.
- [First Stop: The Stoics](https://notimetohurry.com/en/articles/first-stop-the-stoics.html): Second piece — a recorded research dialogue with an AI on Stoicism and slow living: the dichotomy of control, Seneca on time, plus the objections (Marx/Hegel, Aristotle, Nietzsche, Camus).
- [It All Started with a Plate of Pasta](https://notimetohurry.com/en/articles/it-all-started-with-a-plate-of-pasta.html): Third piece — the birth of the movement: Carlo Petrini, a 1986 Rome McDonald's, the 1989 Slow Food manifesto, Cittaslow, McDonaldization, and why the emblem is a snail.
- [About](https://notimetohurry.com/en/about.html): Murat Saydan — 27 years in IT (banking, ~20 years of logistics-sector ERP, then e-commerce and Rivea Beauty), now learning to slow down.
